browser-extension.context: A browser window with a solid jigsaw puzzle piece in the page. Used for extension managers, add-on stores, plugin settings and extension install prompts.

vertical-tabs.context: A browser window with a narrow left column of four stacked tab rows, the top one solid. Marks vertical tab sidebars, tab lists and tree style tab layouts in browsers.

sleeping-tab.context: A browser tab with a crescent moon and a z floating above it. Shows tabs that were put to sleep, suspended or discarded to save memory and battery.

audio-playing-tab.context: A browser tab holding a speaker with two sound waves. Marks a tab that is playing sound, with options to mute it, as seen in tab strips.

too-many-tabs.context: A browser window whose top edge is crowded with a squeezed row of tiny tabs. Used for tab overload, tab hoarding and tab management warnings.

browser-profiles.context: A browser window with two small people side by side in the page. Used for switching browser profiles, work and personal accounts, and multi user browsers.

kiosk-mode.context: A freestanding kiosk with a tall screen showing a full screen page and no toolbar. Marks kiosk mode for locked down public terminals, information displays and digital signage.

web-clipper.context: A small browser window above a dashed cut line with scissors cutting along it. Stands for web clippers that save part of a page, snip articles or capture content for notes.

full-page-screenshot.context: A tall web page inside four camera corner brackets. Used for full page and scrolling screenshots, page capture and snapshot tools.

page-loading-bar.context: A browser window with a partly filled progress bar in the page. Used for page load progress, loading indicators and waiting states.

page-crash.context: A browser window with a crack across the top corner and a sad face in the page. Shown when a tab crashes or a page fails with a browser error.

search-results-page.context: A browser page with a magnifier and query line on top and three stacked result lines. Used for search results pages, search engine listings and result lists.

new-tab-page.context: A browser window with a centered search bar and a grid of six shortcut tiles. Marks the new tab page, start page and speed dial with favorite sites.

mobile-browser.context: A smartphone with an address bar across the top of its screen and page lines below. Used for mobile browsing, mobile web views and phone sized pages.

desktop-site-view.context: A desktop monitor with a small smartphone standing in front of its lower right side. Used for request desktop site toggles and switching from the mobile to the full site.

user-agent.context: A browser window with a small ID card showing a head and two text lines in the page. Stands for the user agent string that identifies a browser to servers, and for request headers.

browser-storage.context: A browser window with a database cylinder in the page. Used for local storage, session storage, cookies and other data kept in the browser.

coming-soon-page.context: A browser window with a small rocket standing in the page. Used for coming soon, pre launch and teaser landing pages.

under-construction-page.context: A browser window with a solid traffic cone on the left and a barrier on the right. Used for under construction pages, unfinished sites and work in progress notices.

maintenance-page.context: A browser window with a wrench and a screwdriver crossed in the page. Shown when a site is down for maintenance or scheduled downtime.

thank-you-page.context: A browser window with a solid heart above a short centered text line. Used for thank you and confirmation pages after a purchase, signup or form submission.

faq-page.context: A browser page with a large question mark and three accordion chevrons beside it. Used for FAQ pages, help centers and expandable question lists.

team-page.context: A browser page with a grid of six small round heads, each with a short name line under it. Used for meet the team, staff and people directory pages.

about-page.context: A browser page with a round portrait on the left and text lines on the right and below. Used for about us, biography and company story pages.

wiki-article.context: An article page with a solid infobox at the right, a heading bar and text lines. Used for encyclopedia style reference articles, wikis and knowledge bases.

discussion-forum.context: A stack of three thread rows, each with a round avatar, a title line and a reply bubble. Used for forums, message boards and discussion topic lists.

comment-section.context: Article text lines above two comment rows with round avatars, the second one indented. Used for comment sections, reader replies and threaded discussion under posts.

blogroll.context: A header bar over three list rows, each with a small solid site tile and a text line. Used for blogrolls, link lists and recommended sites in blog sidebars.

webring.context: A circle of five small web page tiles sitting on a closed ring. Stands for webrings, groups of related sites linked in a loop in the retro web.

visitor-counter.context: A retro counter strip of boxed digit cells with an eye above it. Used for hit counters, page view counts and retro visitor tallies on old style sites.

bulletin-board-system.context: An old boxy monitor with menu lines on its screen and a cable running to a small modem. Stands for dial up bulletin board systems and early online services.

internet-cafe.context: Two screens on stands at a desk with a steaming coffee cup standing between them. Used for internet cafes, cyber cafes and public computer rental spots.

web-portal.context: A browser window with an open arched doorway in the page and an arrow passing through it. Used for web portals, gateways and entry points into a site or service.

web-archive.context: An archive box with the edges of stacked web pages standing up out of its open top. Used for web archives, saved page snapshots and website preservation.

web-directory.context: An open index book with a small globe on the left page and tabs down the right edge. Used for web directories, site catalogs and categorized link listings.

extranet.context: A tall office building and a shorter partner building joined by a line that crosses a dashed boundary. Stands for extranets that give partners limited access to a company network.

captive-portal.context: A wifi symbol above a small browser window showing a wide sign in button. Marks captive portals, the sign in or accept terms page shown by guest and hotel wifi.

internet-service-provider.context: A building with an antenna mast on its roof and a cable running across to a small house. Used for ISPs, broadband companies and home internet service.

net-neutrality.context: An equals sign above three parallel lines of equal width, each carrying one data block. Stands for net neutrality, the idea that all traffic is treated equally.

geo-restriction.context: A globe with a lowered barrier arm and post crossing in front of it. Used for geo blocking, region locked content and not available in your country messages.

web-filter.context: A funnel sitting on a browser window with a few dots caught inside it. Used for web filtering, parental controls, URL blocklists and safe browsing tools.

bot-traffic.context: A small robot head with an arrow cursor pointing into a browser window next to it. Used for bot traffic, crawlers, scrapers and automated visits in analytics.

internet-exchange-point.context: A central square hub with six spokes running out to small dots and squares around it. Stands for internet exchange points where networks meet and share traffic.

port-forwarding.context: A router box with two antennas and an arrow leading from it to a small door on the right. Used for port forwarding, NAT rules and opening a port to reach a device or server.

traffic-surge.context: A server rack with three arrows pressing in from the left and a zigzag heat line above it. Used for traffic spikes, overloaded servers and sudden high demand.

digital-divide.context: Two houses side by side with a dashed gap between them, only the left one with a wifi signal above. Stands for the digital divide, unequal access to internet and technology.

internet-shutdown.context: A globe with a power plug pulled away from its wall socket beside it. Used for internet shutdowns, blackouts and network outages.

web-surfing.context: A surfboard riding a wave with a small arrow cursor above it. Used for surfing the web, casual browsing and wave themed internet content.

doomscrolling.context: A smartphone with a weary face on the first feed card, more cards below and a long down arrow beside it. Used for doomscrolling, endless feeds and phone overuse.

online-voting.context: A browser window with a ballot paper dropping into a ballot box in the page. Used for online voting, e-voting and digital elections.

online-auction.context: A browser window with an auction gavel striking its sound block in the page. Used for online auctions, bidding sites and sold notices.

cross-site-scripting.context: A browser window with angle brackets and a slash typed into an input field. Used for cross site scripting (XSS), script injection and web security flaws.

web-application-firewall.context: A shield with a brick pattern across it. Used for web application firewalls, request filtering and protecting a site from attacks.

typosquatting.context: An address bar with a text line and a mismatched character, with a fishing hook hanging from its end. Used for typosquatting, lookalike domains and misspelled URL traps.

content-security-policy.context: A browser window with a small shield on the left and three ticked lines on the right. Used for content security policy headers and lists of approved sources.

website-defacement.context: A browser window with a spray can and a scribbled squiggle across the page. Used for defaced and hacked websites and online vandalism.

dark-pattern.context: A dialog box with a large solid accept button and a tiny close cross tucked in the corner. Used for dark patterns, deceptive design and manipulative interface choices.

interstitial-ad.context: A browser window fully covered by an ad panel with a small countdown ring and two text lines. Used for interstitial and full page ads that appear before content.

skyscraper-ad.context: A browser window with a tall narrow solid ad down the right side beside lines of text. Used for skyscraper banners, sidebar ads and vertical display ad units.

pay-per-click.context: An arrow cursor clicking on a coin. Used for pay per click advertising, cost per click and paid search ads.

retargeting-ad.context: A person silhouette and an ad card joined by a curved arrow that loops back over the top. Used for retargeting and remarketing ads that follow past visitors.

ad-network.context: A central node linked by lines to four small browser windows, each holding a solid ad block. Used for ad networks, ad exchanges and publisher advertising platforms.

clickbait.context: A headline card with a hook dangling on a line above it and a big exclamation mark beside the hook. Used for clickbait headlines and misleading sensational titles.

cookie-wall.context: A cookie with a bite taken out standing above a brick wall. Used for cookie walls, consent gates and cookie banners that block a page until accepted.

paywall.context: A browser window with two text lines above and a brick wall with a coin slot across its lower half. Used for paywalls and subscription gates on articles.

members-area.context: A browser window with a membership card showing a star and a small avatar. Used for members areas, member portals and subscriber only sections.

affiliate-link.context: A chain link with a small coin attached to its lower right end. Used for affiliate and referral links that earn a commission.

utm-tag.context: An address bar with three small tags hanging from it on short strings. Used for UTM tags, campaign tracking parameters and tagged URLs.

deep-link.context: A chain link above an arrow that dives into a stack of layered app screens. Used for deep links, universal links and links that open a specific screen inside an app.

jump-link.context: A page with a solid hash sign at the top left and a curved arrow jumping down to a heading bar. Used for jump links, anchor links and table of contents links within a page.

link-building.context: A small rising wall of solid bricks with a chain link resting on top. Used for link building, earning backlinks and off page SEO work.

anchor-text.context: A line of text with one underlined word and a chain link above that word. Used for anchor text, the clickable words of a hyperlink.

internal-links.context: A browser window with three small page blocks joined to each other by a link path. Used for internal links between pages of the same site and site link structure.

toxic-link.context: A chain link above a small skull. Used for toxic backlinks, spam links and dangerous or malicious URLs.

link-equity.context: A chain link with a water drop falling from it onto a small page below. Used for link equity, link juice and the value a link passes to another page.

link-farm.context: Three upright chain loops on stems growing from a ground line like crops. Used for link farms, spam link schemes and bulk link networks.

link-exchange.context: Two pages at opposite corners with two curved arrows swapping between them. Used for reciprocal link exchanges and link swaps between sites.

canonical-url.context: Three small page tabs with arrows pointing to one main page that wears a crown. Used for canonical URLs, the preferred address among duplicate pages.

redirect-chain.context: Three pages in a row joined by two curved arrows hopping from one to the next. Used for redirect chains, repeated hops before reaching a final URL.

redirect-loop.context: Two small pages facing each other joined by two curved arrows that form an endless circle. Used for redirect loops and too many redirects errors.
